observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.addAll attempts to copy elements from two input arrays into a new array using System.arraycopy. When the input arrays have incompatible types (e.g., Integer[] and Long[]), System.arraycopy throws an ArrayStoreException, which is an unhandled runtime exception that crashes the operation.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is the lack of a validation check to ensure that the component types of the two input arrays are compatible before attempting the array copy. The method assumes that the arrays can be merged into an array of the type of the first array, but it fails to verify this assumption. Adding a check to validate type compatibility and throwing an appropriate exception (like IllegalArgumentException) would prevent the ArrayStoreException and satisfy the requirement for clearer error handling.
evidence_used: java.lang.ArrayStoreException: arraycopy: type mismatch: can not copy java.lang.Long[] into java.lang.Integer[]

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves an interface contract (the method signature implies it can handle T[] and T..., but fails on type mismatch), the primary mechanism is the missing validation of the input parameters before performing the operation.
The algorithm itself is correct for compatible types; the failure is due to the lack of a guard condition to handle incompatible types.
